title_options: Qwen3 0.6B as an Agent Tool Router: 13 CPU Calls, 10-94 s Each
Qwen3 0.6B Agent Tool Router on CPU: Right Tool, 94 s Worst Case
A 0.6B Tool Router on CPU: 13 Measured Calls, 128-Token Truncation
presentation.title_rationale: The selected title names the product first (Qwen3 0.6B), states the reader's actual question (can this model route agent tool calls) and answers it with the two numbers that decide the case: the number of measured calls and the 10-94 s per-call spread. It avoids claiming an accuracy rate, since the fixture has 7 non-truncated calls and no observed wrong tool.
presentation.visual_purpose: The cover plots all 13 measured calls as one lane each: horizontal position is wall time in seconds, and the marker shape/colour separates calls that returned create_ticket with valid arguments from calls that returned nothing because the 128-token budget was exhausted. It shows the two facts the body turns into a decision - the latency spread at each registry size and the truncation signature - using only values present in results.jsonl; it is not a benchmark of the model and covers one host, 1/4/8 tools and 2-3 samples per cell.

corrections_applied.change: cover.alt rewritten to describe the rendered figure: filled blue circles = the 7 calls that returned create_ticket with valid title/priority (done_reason=stop), filled orange squares = the 6 no-call calls at the 128-token budget (done_reason=length), each marker labelled with its own wall time; the claims about hollow markers and marked medians are removed. The PNG was not regenerated.

The over-generalised sentence in the wall-time section is replaced with the cell-by-cell restatement from summary.csv: 4-tool median 11.91 s is 7.53 s below the 1-tool median 19.44 s despite 128 more prompt tokens, 8-tool median 32.54 s is 13.10 s above it with a 10.94-94.35 s range, and with three to five samples per cell neither direction supports a per-tool-count latency effect. The same paragraph's 'two to five samples' and the limitations bullet's 'two to three calls per cell' were aligned to the recorded 3 / 5 / 5 calls per registry size.

The 'sampling' parenthetical no longer claims num_predict is recorded per row; it points to the append-time split in the note, and the note's boundary now names the verified timestamps (nine 128-token rows up to 08:28:16Z, four 512-token rows from 08:29:07Z) checked against results.jsonl. results.jsonl was not modified (hash 6551c175...).
